title: Shin: Teeth, Destroy (ancient pictograph to S, Sh)
summary: Teaches the Hebrew letter shin (sounds Sh, S; value 300; meaning Teeth, Destroy) in three different letter shapes, then shows the ancient teeth pictograph changing into a later upright S-like form and then into the modern S(h).

letters.meaning: teeth, destroy (teeth pictograph); sounds Sh, S

numbers.note: gematria value of the letter shin

pictures.description: Small ancient (paleo-Hebrew) shin pictograph: a black wavy line with two humps like teeth, over a black underline, placed between 300 and Teeth, Destroy.
Three-step letter evolution: the large ancient teeth pictograph of shin over a black underline, an arrow to a later upright S-shaped curved form, and an arrow to the large black letters S(h).

uncertain: The three shin shapes at the top are different typefaces/styles; the slide gives no caption for them.
